date_convention: Signed civil years; no year zero. Year-only endpoints suppress beginning with the following civil year; exact documented dates remain exact. These are negative display guards, not a complete validity database.
meaning: Remove known chronological contradictions from both source observations and reference-held maps. A passing guard does not verify boundaries, ownership or an entity’s complete lifespan. Suppressed territory stays unassigned; no invented successor map.

rules.note: Annual limit follows the end of Achaemenid rule in 330 BCE; source borders are not transferred to Alexander.
Seleucid rule ended in 64 BCE; the final year remains year-precision.
No Parthian imperial association is retained after its terminal year, 224 CE.
Last Sasanian ruler Yazdgard III died in 651. This is a conservative latest bound, not a claim of unchanged control through that year.
Republican map associations are not retained beyond the conventional transition to the principate in 27 BCE.
Uses the conventional 476 CE termination of western imperial government. Does not end eastern Roman continuity.
The fall of Constantinople on 29 May 1453 ends this imperial association; successor states require their own geometries.
Western Han and Eastern Han are separated by the Xin interregnum. The museum provides years, so no exact transition day is inferred.
The imperial Tang association is not carried beyond 907.
The preceding Sui dynasty ended in 618; a 700 source label is chronologically incompatible.
Ends the imperial Ming overview after 1644. Southern Ming resistance is a separate political situation and is not represented by holding these borders.
No Mauryan imperial association is retained after 185 BCE; a 100 BCE label is incompatible. Foundation is approximate, so this guard does not impose an exact founding date.
The imperial overview ends after the 1532 conquest watershed. This intentionally does not reuse empire-wide borders for the distinct Vilcabamba resistance state (1536–1572).

sources.title: Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi — Museum of the War of Independence

rules.note: Sultanate abolished on 1 November 1922; no old Ottoman borders are reassigned to the Republic of Turkey.

sources.title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1989–1992, Volume XXXI, Preface

rules.note: Conservative year-end cutoff for dissolution in December 1991, not an assertion of intact control throughout the final month.
The GDR acceded to the Federal Republic on 3 October 1990. West Germany is a period-specific display label, not a claim that the Federal Republic ceased to exist.
INAH dates the city and state to 50–650 CE. Source territory remains an unverified overview.
INAH identifies Monte Albán as a Zapotec capital from the start of the Common Era to 800 CE. Later occupation and sacred use do not imply continuous state government.

sources.title: British Museum collection record: British occupation of Benin City in 1897

rules.note: Applies only to source observations through 1900 for the Benin kingdom in present-day Nigeria; never to modern Republic of Benin.
Revolution in 1911 and abdication in early 1912. Conservative end-of-year bound; no claim that imperial control remained intact throughout 1912.
Mongol Empire established in 1206; source attribution in 1200 is premature. This rule intentionally imposes no unsupported dissolution cutoff.

The research database dates the imperial polity from 320 CE. The 300 CE imperial attribution is excluded; preceding local Gupta rulers are a different scope. No terminal cutoff is inferred from art-period dates.

sources.title: Nile and Newcomers: A Fresh Installation of Egyptian Ptolemaic Art

rules.note: Cleopatra VII’s death and Roman annexation in 30 BCE end the Ptolemaic period.
Capture of Cuauhtémoc and fall of the Mexica capital on 13 August 1521 end this imperial overview; Indigenous population and communities continue.
South Sudan seceded on 9 July 2011. Old united-Sudan geometry is suppressed after partition; this does not assert Sudan ceased to exist. Updated north/south borders require separate sourced polygons.

sources.title: The Art of the Mamluk Period (1250–1517)

rules.note: The Mamluk sultanate ended with Ottoman conquest in 1517. Surviving Mamluk elites do not prolong its independent territorial map.

sources.title: The Art of the Timurid Period (ca. 1370–1507)

rules.note: The Central Asian and Iranian Timurid period ends in 1507. Timur’s death in 1405 is not an end date for the dynasty; Mughal descent does not prolong these territorial polygons.

sources.title: The Art of the Fatimid Period (909–1171)

rules.note: Fatimid caliphal rule ended in 1171. Cairo and its inhabitants continued under successor governments.

sources.title: The Art of the Ilkhanid Period (1256–1353)

rules.note: The united Ilkhanid dynasty fragmented after Abu Saʿid’s death in 1335. Later claimants and artistic continuity do not justify carrying forward one unified imperial polygon.

sources.title: Delhi Sultanate: Political and cultural history

rules.note: The source attribution in 1200 predates the sultanate established in 1206; the Lodi sultanate ended with Babur’s conquest in 1526.
This display scope follows the conventional 962–1806 chronology; earlier Carolingian imperial traditions are distinct. Dissolution does not transfer all imperial territory to Austria.
Goryeo’s dynasty was replaced by Joseon in 1392; Korean population and institutions were not erased.
Silla rule ended in 935. No precise foundation guard is inferred from the traditional 57 BCE origin date.
Rome destroyed Punic Carthage in 146 BCE. The later Roman city is not a continuation of the independent Punic state.
The Tokugawa shogunate ended in the 1868 political transition. The generic label Japan is deliberately not governed by this dynasty-specific rule.
The Kamakura regime was overthrown in 1333. Continuing imperial government at Kyoto and later shogunates do not prolong this regime.
The capital was destroyed in 1767. Later Siamese kingdoms at other capitals do not inherit this exact city-centered territorial assertion.

sources.title: The Act of the Union of Lublin document
The Union of Lublin: The Longest Lasting Union in European History

rules.note: The Commonwealth was established by the Union of Lublin in 1569 and ended with the 1795 partition; the earlier dynastic union is a separate political phase.

sources.title: The Art of the Seljuq Period in Anatolia (1081–1307)

rules.note: This source label lies in Anatolia and denotes the Seljuq Sultanate of Rum, not a caliphate. Its last dynastic phase ended in 1307/1308; the source’s 1400 appearance is anachronistic. No successor border is invented.

sources.title: China Timeline: Western and Eastern Jin; Northern Wei succession

rules.note: The atlas label names the unified Tuoba/Northern Wei dynasty. Its division in 534–535 ends that state; a conservative annual guard starts after 535. Eastern and Western Wei remain separate identities.
Mongol conquest ends the Xixia imperial dynasty in 1227. No 1038 start guard is imposed on the generic label without reviewing whether the 1000 source means a Tangut predecessor.

sources.title: Editorial Foreword: Cham narratives and the 1832 annexation

rules.note: Annexation of the last autonomous principality in 1832 supplies the terminal political limit. This does not end Cham communities, languages or religious life.

source_date_audit.finding: The retained upstream index contains no additional historical snapshots within the current 3000 BCE–2010 CE range. Filling those gaps requires another source or explicit research, not interpolated factual borders.

admission_reviews.label: Chile
admission_reviews.reason: The generic modern-name cutoff accidentally excluded this independent state before 1914. Chile declared independence in 1818. Retained original source geometry can be displayed as source-attributed political association.

admission_reviews.label: Teotihuacan
admission_reviews.reason: INAH identifies a city and state in 50–650 CE. Only existing snapshots within that interval are admitted; borders remain source-attributed.

admission_reviews.label: Monte Albán
admission_reviews.reason: INAH identifies a Zapotec capital from the start of the Common Era to 800 CE. Admit retained political association within that interval, not earlier or later city occupation.
